title: private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
Incident notes - Private deploy networking (VPC peering / DNS / TLS / egress)

Summary:
- Customer private deployment intermittent failures when calling external services and internal service discovery returns NXDOMAIN for some hosts. Symptoms: TLS handshake failures to upstreams, DNS resolution failures for private hostnames, and 'No route to host' from certain subnets.
- Impact: control-plane syncs failing for a subset of on-prem clusters; customers report degraded inference latency and occasional 503s.
- First detected: 2026-02-18 09:05 PST via monitoring alert (route-sync errors, DNS lookup error rate spike).

Timeline / breadcrumbs (local notes):
- 2026-02-18 09:05 - Alert: route-sync job failing in customer-vpc-a (error: "failed to connect to control-plane endpoint: TLS handshake timeout").
- 2026-02-18 09:12 - Confirmed via logs on control-plane: repeated DNSError for service.private.redwood.local (NXDOMAIN).
- 2026-02-18 09:25 - First attempts to reproduce from Bastion in customer VPC (10.0.0.0/16).
- 2026-02-18 09:28 - Opened INC-4321 and pinged Slack channel #private-deployments for triage.
- 2026-02-18 10:00 - Eng on-call (Leah) joined. Began collecting packet captures and IAM/route info.
- 2026-02-18 11:40 - Applied temporary NAT egress rule for control-plane to test external TLS calls; partial improvement observed for metadata endpoints but not for private service discovery.

Commands tried + outputs (copied from bastion):
- Check VPC peering status:
  $ aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=redwood-peer-* --query 'VpcPeeringConnections[*].{Id:VpcPeeringConnectionId,Status:Status.Code}'
  ["VpcPeeringConnectionId: pcx-0a1b2c3d4e", "Status: active"]

- Verify peering routes (route tables attached to customer subnets):
  $ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc123 --query 'RouteTables[*].Routes'
  ... found route for 10.2.0.0/16 via pcx-0a1b2c3d4e in rtb-0aa111, BUT rtb-0bb222 (attached to worker subnets) missing that route -> likely asymmetric routing for some subnets.

- DNS check (internal resolver at 10.0.0.2):
  $ dig @10.0.0.2 service.private.redwood.local A +short
  (no output) -> NXDOMAIN in many queries

  $ dig @10.0.0.2 _service._tcp.service.private.redwood.local SRV +short
  (no output)

- Packet capture: DNS queries leaving bastion but no answers returned from peered VPC resolver IP (10.2.0.2)
  $ sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 53 -w dns.pcap
  Observed UDP queries to 10.2.0.2 but no UDP responses; retrying over TCP shows connection reset.

- TLS test to an upstream service in peered VPC (10.2.4.5:443):
  $ curl --resolve api.private.redwood:443:10.2.4.5 https://api.private.redwood/health -v --max-time 10
  * Connected to 10.2.4.5 (10.2.4.5) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS handshake timeout
  > curl: (28) Operation timed out after 10001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received

  $ openssl s_client -connect 10.2.4.5:443 -servername api.private.redwood -brief
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  139774...:error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol
  ---
  no peer certificate available

- Kernel/network diagnostics on affected worker host: 
  $ ip route show table main | grep 10.2.0.0
  (some hosts missing a route for 10.2.0.0/16 -> default to internet gateway)
  $ sudo iptables -S | grep -i DROP
  (no obvious DROP rules)
  $ sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward -> 1 (expected)

Hypotheses so far:
1) Route table asymmetry: Some subnets' route tables aren't propagating the peering route -> traffic egressing to IGW instead of peering, causing DNS and TLS traffic to hit firewall/NAT and be dropped.
2) DNS resolver/forwarding broken across peering: If the resolver in peered VPC is only reachable from certain AZs or subnets, requests from affected subnets may be dropped. Observed UDP queries with no responses and TCP resets suggests middlebox / firewall dropping DNS responses or MTU/fragmentation issues.
3) Security group / NACL blocking ephemeral ports for DNS over TCP or TLS ephemeral ports -> TLS handshake doesn't complete.
4) Overlapping CIDR / incorrect route selection: small overlap with a vendor-managed network caused AWS to reject route propagation for some route tables.
5) TLS SNI mismatch / ALPN mismatch - openssl output shows unsupported protocol on raw connection; could be TCP-level proxied connection that doesn't speak TLS (maybe a proxy expecting PROXY protocol or mTLS).

Mitigations applied (notes):
- 2026-02-18 11:40 - Added temporary route to rtb-0bb222 for 10.2.0.0/16 via pcx-0a1b2c3d4e; immediate recovery for worker nodes in that subnet (route-sync succeeded).
- 2026-02-18 12:10 - Reconfigured resolver policy: forced use of TCP for DNS queries from bastion to peered resolver to test behavior; observed fewer timeouts but still occasional resets.
- 2026-02-18 12:35 - Temporarily allowed all egress on worker security groups to verify SG/NACL were not the limiter; no change for DNS failures.
- 2026-02-18 13:05 - Replaced Transit Gateway attachment (customer uses TGW) with fresh attachment to clear stuck associations (ticket opened with cloud provider).

Observations / evidence to capture for postmortem:
- Route table snapshot for all subnets (rtb-0aa111, rtb-0bb222, rtb-0cc333) before/after change.
- tcpdump pcap of DNS traffic from an affected worker (dns.pcap) showing queries and missing UDP replies.
- curl/openssl logs showing TLS handshake failures (attached as tls-fail.log).
- AWS describe outputs (VPC peering, TGW attachments, route tables) saved to S3 location: s3://incident-dumps/INC-4321/2026-02-18/
- Slack thread link and timestamps for on-call decisions.

Open questions / next investigative steps:
- Reproduce locally: Can we repro from a container in the same subnet (worker) vs the bastion? Need to run tcpdump on both endpoints and compare.
- Confirm if DNS responses were received by peered resolver but dropped before reaching requester (capture on resolver side).
- Check for MTU or fragmentation: run ping -M do -s 1472 to upstream to see if fragmenting causes UDP DNS loss.
- Confirm vendor firewall / partner config: ask infra team if any middlebox between peered VPCs doing DPI or ACLs.
- Validate TLS path is directly to service or through a proxy (we saw unsupported protocol on s_client -> maybe connecting to a proxy expecting PROXY protocol or mTLS handshake).

Post-incident follow-ups (owners / rough ETA):
- Route table audit across customer VPCs (owner: Noah) - due 2026-02-22
- DNS resolver logs capture + analysis (owner: Eliot) - due 2026-02-20
- TGW / peering architecture review and diagram to catch asymmetric routing (owner: Samira) - due 2026-02-26
- Update runbook: include early checks for route propagation, resolver reachability, and simple curl/openssl probe commands (owner: Leah) - due 2026-03-01

Notes to self / informal reminders:
- When capturing openssl output, try -msg to see handshake messages.
- Keep a copy of the temporary route added so we can revert after a clean fix.
- Include port ranges for DNS TCP (53) and ephemeral ports in the runbook.

Slack/communication highlights:
- @leah-wong: confirmed temporary route fixed route-sync for 2 subnets
- @noah-gomez: filing TGW support ticket with provider; provided TGW attachment ids

Raw artifacts saved:
- s3://incident-dumps/INC-4321/2026-02-18/dns.pcap
- s3://incident-dumps/INC-4321/2026-02-18/tls-fail.log
- s3://incident-dumps/INC-4321/2026-02-18/aws-describe-output.json

-- end of notes (draft)
